notes: 3 runs per configuration per eval (24 runs). The with-skill pass rate was 99% against 83% without, a gain of 15 points. That matches iteration 1's +16 from single runs, so the effect is consistent.

Consistent wins: every with-skill README said who the project is for (0/3 baselines did). Every with-skill how-to used a real numbered list with condition-first steps (0/3 baselines; they used '## Step N' headings). Every with-skill release-notes run left out commit hashes and internal commits (1/3 baselines). Reviews: the skill flagged the missing audience in 2/3 runs (baseline 0/3), and its findings were ranked by impact in 3/3 (baseline 1/3).
The only with-skill miss: review run 2's revised draft added a 'Who this project is for' section, but none of its listed findings named that gap.

These checks never separate the two: template leftovers, invented flags, env vars and URLs, Apache-2.0 licence, pip/Python 3.14 install, token-location facts, and breaking/feature/fix coverage in the release notes. Both configurations pass them every time, so they guard against regressions without measuring the skill.
Cost: the skill added 13s (+39%) and about 12.6k tokens (+32%) per run, from reading the TGDP guide and template. With-skill time varies more (±16.7s); one review run took 90s.

Things graders noticed that no expectation checks yet (candidates for iteration 3): two rotation how-tos print the secret with `echo $TIDYFEED_TOKEN`; a release note suggests `pip install --upgrade tidyfeed` although nothing says it's on an index; README sections containing only HTML TODO comments render as empty headings; one release note says 'three breaking changes' and then lists four; and 'ranked by impact' passes any High/Medium/Low grouping.
